Buccaneers 38, Seahawks 35: Recap | Instant Reaction | Box score Two teams with two stout defenses turned a potential low-scoring affair into a shootout between two quarterbacks who, coincidentally, once spent time on the same roster in Carolina. In the end, it was Baker Mayfield who outdueled his former teammate Sam Darnold. Or was it Darnold who outdueled himself by throwing a late interception ? Or, wait, was the fight lost when Seattle’s defense couldn’t stop the Bucs from returning blow for blow? Turns out a surprising game left some confusing takeaways. Here’s the good and bad of each. Darnold’s stellar outing ended with heartbreak, but should leave you feeling encouraged. Darnold technically didn’t make the pass that mattered most, which I suppose you could say for any pass that’s intercepted with less than a minute remaining from your own 38-yard line. But he made a lot of passes that really mattered, and that’s encouraging for a Seahawks offense that entered the season with the expectation that Darnold would be a lesser version of his 2024 self. Darnold’s final line (28 for 34, 341 yards, four touchdowns, one interception) isn’t going to reflect the bit of luck he got away with in the fourth, nor the brilliance from a few of his shots. A pass nearly tipped for what would’ve been a pick six took another bounce into the air and fell into the waiting arms of Cooper Kupp. There’s some luck for you. But a 53-yarder to a sprinting Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had a defender on his hip? Evading pressure on fourth down to toss a touchdown to rookie Tory Horton? Those were clutch plays, and there were more from the offense in the second half, and it deserves a fair share of credit even with a loss. Made it look easy. 😤 Darnold to JSN for 53 yards. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/aPg0aP9s9A — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 5, 2025 That's how you answer on fourth. 😮‍💨 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/I9tppE8WmF — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 5, 2025 It really makes the final pick a shame. “At the end of the day I’ve gotta protect the football in that situation,” Darnold told reporters after the game, doling out credit to the Bucs’ defense. He felt he should’ve changed the protection pre-snap. “That was bad quarterback play on that last snap.” The Bucs were short a few defenders of their own, including a starting and a backup cornerback. They kept a lid on Seattle’s offense through most of the first half but allowed 311 yards from the Seahawks in the second half alone. “Just crushing,” Kupp said of the loss, a line that perfectly summed up the feeling of fans leaving the stadium to waltz next door to T-Mobile Field with prayers that the Mariners could save their season. It’s been a tough weekend for Seattle sports. The Seahawks defense isn’t as bad as their numbers Sunday, but injuries adding up could change that. On to the more confusing and concerning part of the day. The Seahawks were a top scoring defense in the second half of last season. Through four weeks this year they were even better, ranking third in points allowed behind Denver and Houston. They’ve been one of the better defenses against the run and in the red zone this year (46%). That’s a good chunk of time to establish some fairly reliable trends. Sunday might’ve been their worst performance yet under coach Mike Macdonald. Mayfield and the Bucs marched down the field over and over, racking up 426 net yards, 38 points, and going over 60% on both third down and in the red zone. How big a factor are injuries here? The Seahawks entered the day without starting safety Julian Love — a leader on that side of the ball — and starting corner Devon Witherspoon. The defensive line was missing DeMarcus Lawrence. But no matter, the Bucs were without wide receiver Mike Evans and running back Bucky Irving, so all’s fair, right? Easier to say when you’re only short three defenders. The Bucs attacked early, adding just a pair of field goals to start the game but otherwise moving far more easily than previous opponents against this group. By the end of the game the defense was being torched far too frequently. The Bucs didn’t need Irving after all — turns out 56 rushing yards won’t do you in when Mayfield can pass for 370. I don’t think the defense Macdonald rolled out Week 1 is this bad. And we know that — they’ve proven to be a stellar unit so far. But the defense they might have to roll out if these injuries are more concerning? That’s a pretty massive question mark. text_body: Game Report, 2025 Week 6: Seahawks 20, Jaguars 12 Oct 12, 2025 at 04:22 PM John Oehser Jaguars Senior Writer Copied! JACKSONVILLE – The scrap, grit and want-to were there yet again. This time, those weren't enough. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw two touchdowns and the Jaguars inched close late, but what had been reliable wasn't on Sunday – and in a game largely defined by Jaguars mistakes, the Seattle Seahawks held on for a 20-12 victory in front of 61,056 at EverBank Stadium on a sun-splashed October afternoon. "We didn't play our best ball today," Lawrence said. Head Coach Liam Coen called "deflating moments" the "theme of the day." "We will not beat quality teams like this if we continue to hurt ourselves," Coen said. "We continue to hurt ourselves and have these self-inflicted wounds. That ultimately is on me." The Seahawks clinched the victory by kneeling out the final 1:57 on their final drive, with tight end AJ Barner's 61-yard reception from quarterback Sam Darnold giving them possession deep in Jaguars territory. The Jaguars had three possessions in the fourth quarter trailing by eight points – their three series before Seattle's final drive – but produced just one first down on the three drives. "It's on all of us," Lawrence said. "It's all of us taking accountability and fixing the things we can control." After entering Sunday with an NFL-leading 14 takeaways, the Jaguars didn't force one Sunday. The Jaguars, after allowing six sacks in the first five games, allowed seven for 44 yards to the Seahawks. The Seahawks also were credited with 17 hits on Lawrence. "Credit to them: They beat us up up front," Coen said. The Jaguars also were penalized 10 times for 76 yards, with Coen emphasizing that too many of the penalties came at critical times. "We have to look in the mirror and fix the problems that have been there all year," Lawrence said. The Jaguars (4-2) lost after winning three consecutive games, with the Seahawks (4-2) winning for a third time in four games. The Jaguars are 3-1 at EverBank Stadium this season, with Sunday's game extending the Seahawks' road winning streak to nine games. Darnold threw a 61-yard second-quarter touchdown to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and an 11-yard third-quarter touchdown to wide receiver Cooper Kupp to give the Seahawks a 20-6 lead entering the fourth quarter. Lawrence gave the Jaguars an early lead with a first-quarter touchdown pass to wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., then pulled them to within eight points with a touchdown pass to wide receiver Tim Patrick early in the fourth quarter. "Guys fought," cornerback Jourdan Lewis said. "We fought back. It just wasn't good enough." Lawrence completed 27 of 42 passes for 258 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, with running back Travis Etienne Jr. rushing for 27 yards on 12 carries. Brian Thomas Jr. caught eight passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. "Some of the stuff we were doing was working," Thomas said. "We've just got to quit beating ourselves." Darnold completed 16 of 27 passes for 295 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, with running back Kenneth Walker III rushing for 34 yards 10 carries. Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 162 yards and one touchdown. Jaguars kicker Cam Little missed an extra point and a 50-yard field goal in the first half, with the Seahawks leading 10-6 at halftime. The Jaguars not only did not have a takeaway for the first time this season on Sunday, they registered just one sack – by defensive tackle Arik Armstead when the Jaguars blitzed Darnold. The Seahawks managed just 13 first downs, but 122 of their 346 yards came on two long pass plays – to Smith-Nigba and Barner. "They hit enough explosives and we didn't," Coen said. "That's the reality. We didn't get after their quarterback. They got after ours. They hit a couple of big plays in the pass game and we did not. We have to get after their quarterback more as they got after ours." 2025 Week 6, Step by step: Thomas' 21-yard reception from Lawrence gave the Jaguars a 6-0 lead with 1:14 remaining in the first quarter, capping an eight-play, 61-yard drive on which the Jaguars twice converted third downs of more than 10 yards. The Jaguars outgained the Seahawks, 90-36, in the first quarter. Myers' 24-yard field goal cut the lead to 6-3 with 10:38 remaining in the second quarter, with Darnold's 61-yard touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba on the first play of the Seahawks' ensuing series giving them a 10-6 lead with 8:34 remaining in the first half. Myers' 53-yard field goal gave the Seahawks a 13-6 lead with :10 remaining in a second quarter in which they outgained the Jaguars, 136-62. Kupp's 11-yard reception from Darnold extended the Seahawks' lead to 20-6 with 10:14 remaining in the third quarter. Lawrence's 26-yard touchdown pass to Patrick capped a 14-play, 82-yard drive and cut the lead to 20-12 with 13:00 remaining. Notable: Rookie center Jonah Monheim made his first career start with starter Robert Hainsey inactive after sustaining a hamstring injury in a victory over the Kansas City Chiefs last Monday. The Jaguars' other four inactive players Sunday: Running back Cody Schrader, defensive tackle Khalen Saunders Sr., linebacker Yasir Abdullah and safety Kahlef Hailassie. Abdullah missed a third consecutive game with a hamstring injury, with defensive end Travon Walker returning after missing the Chiefs game with a wrist injury. Jaguars rookie guard Wyatt Milum and rookie defensive end Danny Striggow were active for the first time this season, with Milum missing the first five games with a knee injury. Also: cornerback Greg Newsome II – acquired in a trade from the Cleveland Browns on Thursday – was active and played in a reserve role. Injury report: The Jaguars reported no significant injuries Sunday. Seattle Seahawks 20, Jacksonville Jaguars 12: Box Score | Recap The defense piled up seven sacks in a bounce-back win for the Seahawks, who lost Florida’s other team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, in a shootout at home last weekend. Seattle improved to 4-2 with its Week 6 triumph and moved into a three-way tie for first place in the NFC West. Stacy Rost: 3 nuggets from short-handed Seattle Seahawks’ win over Jags Here are the instant reactions to Sunday’s game from some of the voices of Seattle Sports, including Seahawks Radio Network analyst Dave Wyman’s thoughts in the video the at the top of this post. Bob Stelton – Wyman & Bob (2-7 p.m. weekdays) This is a very nice win on the road for the Seattle Seahawks. Jacksonville has been a surprise team coming in with a 4-1 record and, despite being riddled with injuries on defense, the Hawks held the Jags to just 12 points and sacked Trevor Lawrence seven times! Lawrence had only been sacked a total of six times in five games coming into this one. Kudos to Byron Murphy II, who had two sacks on the day and now has 4 1/2 on the season. He had just one-half sack all of last season. Also, a very nice return to the field for Demarcus Lawrence chipping in with 2 1/2 sacks on the day. Another stellar day for Sam Darnold going 16 of 27 for 295 yards and two touchdowns. It was almost a 50-50 split between run and pass on the day – 27 pass attempts to 26 run attempts. Really the only negative offensively was their inability to get that run game going, coming away with just 60 total yards on those 26 carries. Other than that, there’s a lot to be excited about on a day where this team went on the road very short-handed on defense and beat a team that has been rolling. Watch out for Byron 👀 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/LaMVqmmXjs — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Brock Huard – Brock & Salk (6-10 a.m. weekdays) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Seattle Sports (@seattlesports710) Mike Lefko – Wyman & Bob Game ball to the Seattle Seahawks’ defensive line for setting the tone early and stepping up to help a secondary dealing with injury attrition. Trevor Lawrence had only been sacked six times total in five games coming into this one, but the Seahawks defensive front got to him early and helped rack up a season-high seven on the day. Sam Darnold has continued to play like one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. His feathery throw to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 61-yard TD flipped momentum early in the game, and he made one of the biggest plays of the day with his third-down touchdown strike to Cooper Kupp. The Seahawks’ lack of a run game made for another adventure when trying to close out a game again. They couldn’t hold a lead against the Cardinals, and this one became a little too close for comfort today. For as good as Darnold has been, it becomes very difficult to take significant chunks of time off the clock when your offense is one-dimensional. After one-third of the season, the absence of a sustained rushing attack looms as the biggest issue for the Seahawks’ offense. On the other side of the ball, you hope that an extra day before the Monday night game against the Texans and then a bye week after are the balm for all the injuries ailing your key players in the secondary. COOP there it is! 🔥 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/2dutCTETMx — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Observations from Seattle Seahawks’ 20-12 win over Jaguars

(AP) — Having thrown a combined six interceptions in his last two starts in Jacksonville, Sam Darnold refused to get greedy this time around. Seattle Seahawks 20, Jacksonville Jaguars 12: Box Score He played it safe and ended up with a turnover-free performance. Darnold threw for 295 yards, with touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp , and the Seattle Seahawks dominated both lines of scrimmage on their way to a 20-12 victory against the Jaguars on Sunday. “I told myself I was going to take what they give me, and if they give me a checkdown, take it,” said Darnold, whose late interception last week proved costly against Tampa Bay. “I felt like I did a pretty good job of that.” Smith-Njigba finished with eight catches for 162 yards as the Seahawks (4-2) rebounded from a last-second loss to the Buccaneers and improved to 22-6 over the last decade in 1 p.m. kickoffs on the East Coast. The Jaguars (4-2), meanwhile, looked every bit like a team that spent the week reveling in a Monday night victory against three-time AFC champion Kansas City. Jacksonville’s first three snaps set the tone: a sack, a holding penalty and a 3-yard loss. The Jags were penalized 10 times for 76 yards. Trevor Lawrence was sacked a season-high seven times. Travis Etienne was held to 27 yards on 12 carries. Brian Thomas Jr. dropped a third-down pass late with no defenders on him. And the Jaguars had a 54-yard TD pass from Lawrence to Thomas nullified because rookie Travis Hunter lined up offsides. “It’s an undisciplined operation at the moment,” coach Liam Coen said. “What’s standing in our way? Right now, it’s us.” . @TankLawrence came through SWINGING. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/wjR4kfb1mR — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Jacksonville still made it close in the fourth quarter following Lawrence’s 26-yard TD pass to Tim Patrick. It helped that Seattle went 1 for 11 on third downs. But the Seahawks sealed it by forcing three punts in the fourth and then Darnold connected with tight end AJ Barner for a 61-yarder , which allowed them to run out the clock after another penalty on Jacksonville. He made that look wayyy too easy. 🔥 @_ajbarner_ for 61 yards. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/VCEt8fCDPi — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 “We obviously didn’t play our best ball,” Lawrence said. “A lot of mistakes. A lot of self-inflicted wounds like we’ve talked about in the past. We’ve got to clean it up.” It was the first time this season that the Jaguars failed to notch a takeaway. They entered the week leading the league with 14. “That was critical,” Seattle coach Mike Macdonald said. “We knew they would do that going into the game. They’re an opportunistic team. The numbers speak for themselves. I thought our ball security was tremendous.” Newsome burned on his first snap with Jacksonville Newly acquired Jaguars cornerback Greg Newsome made a less-than-ideal first impression. Smith-Njigba torched Newsome for a 61-yard TD reception on Newsome’s first snap with Jacksonville. “I knew (Newsome was in the game),” Smith-Njigba said. “But that was good to take advantage of that look and execute.” The Jaguars traded cornerback Tyson Campbell for Newsome on Wednesday night. Someone hit rewind. 61-yards to the end zone. 🔥 @jaxon_smith1 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/K2SywHB46G — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Wesley Hines-Allen serves as an honorary captain Jaguars defensive end and team captain Josh Hines-Allen had a special helper for the coin toss. Hines-Allen brought his 8-year-old son, Wesley, to midfield as part of the NFL’s “Crucial Catch” program, which is dedicated to fighting cancer and saving lives. Wesley was an honorary captain two months after completing treatment for pediatric cancer. Wesley was diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia in December and underwent chemotherapy for six months. Key injuries Seattle Seahawks: DT Jarran Reed injured his left leg in the fourth quarter. The Seahawks played without three starting defensive backs: S Julian Love and CBs Devon Witherspoon and CB Tariq Woolen. Jaguars: LB Devin Lloyd felt “a little tight,” but the team never reported an injury and later said he was on the bench because of a coaches’ decision. DE Travon Walker was active less than two weeks after having wrist surgery. He played mostly on passing downs while wearing a club on his left hand. Up next The Seahawks stay in the AFC South and host Houston next Monday night. The Jaguars “host” the Los Angeles Rams at Wembley Stadium in London next Sunday. text_body: SEATTLE SEAHAWKS Observations from Seahawks’ 20-12 win over Jaguars Oct 12, 2025, 2:30 PM | Updated: 9:57 pm Seahawks Re-Sign Rashid Shaheed + Free Agency Departures & News - REACTION Hosts Dave Wyman and Bob Stelton (Wyman & Bob) to discuss the news of the first day of NFL Free agency for the Seattle Seahawks, Including the Seahawks resigning Rashid Shaheed and Josh Jobe. They were coming off a difficult last-second loss the week prior. And they were traveling some 2,400 miles across the country to face a surging 4-1 team in a game that kicked off at 10 a.m. Pacific time. No problem. The Seahawks simply did what they’ve done so often under second-year head coach Mike Macdonald – win on the road. Instant reaction | Recap | Box score Seattle beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-12 on Sunday to improve to 4-2 on the season. It was the Seahawks’ ninth straight road victory and it improved them to 10-1 on the road under Macdonald. Here are three things that stood out from Seattle’s latest triumph away from home. JSN continues his tear By this point, it’s become clear. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has emerged as one of the league’s top wide receivers. The third-year Seattle wideout had another monster game, recording eight catches for 162 yards and a touchdown – including five catches for 117 yards and a TD by the midway point of the second quarter. It bumped Smith-Njigba’s season total to 696 receiving yards, which is the 15th-most by any NFL player through his team’s first six games since the 1970 NFL merger, according to Stathead . Smith-Njigba’s biggest play came on a 61-yard TD catch midway through the second quarter, when he raced past newly acquired cornerback Greg Newsome II and hauled in a perfectly placed deep ball from Sam Darnold for the longest reception of his career. Smith-Njigba also had catches of 35 and 32 yards, which gives him an NFL-high eight receptions of 30-plus yards this season. Touchdown JSN! 61 yards. SEAvsJAX on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/2RqhCoOuX4 — NFL (@NFL) October 12, 2025 Seattle’s pass rush takes over With the Seahawks down three key players in their secondary – two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Devon Witherspoon, veteran safety Julian Love and cornerback Riq Woolen – they needed a bounceback performance up front after mustering only one sack in last week’s 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The pass rush delivered in a massive way. Seattle applied constant pressure on Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence and piled up a season-high seven sacks – which was especially impressive considering the Jaguars had allowed just six sacks through their first five games. DeMarcus Lawrence and Byron Murphy II led the way with 2.0 sacks apiece, Uchenna Nwosu recorded 1.5 sacks, linebacker Drake Thomas added a sack on a blitz and Leonard Williams was credited with a half-sack. . @TankLawrence came through SWINGING. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/wjR4kfb1mR — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Moreover, two of the sacks came in particularly pivotal moments. Late in the first half, DeMarcus Lawrence took down Trevor Lawrence for a 9-yard loss that created a longer field-goal attempt for Jacksonville kicker Cam Little, who then sailed his ensuing 50-yard attempt wide of the right upright. And with the Seahawks holding an eight-point lead with less than 4 minutes left in the game, Lawrence and Nwosu combined for a third-down sack that forced Jacksonville to punt. The Jaguars never got the ball back after that. Hawks close it out For as well as the Seahawks have played this season, they’ve had issues closing out games. In their Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, they blew a late four-point lead by surrendering a go-ahead TD drive in the closing minutes. In last week’s loss to the Buccaneers, they blew a late seven-point lead by giving up a game-tying TD drive and then handing the ball right back to Tampa Bay on a costly interception that set up the Bucs’ game-winning field goal. And in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, they blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead before rebounding to win on a last-second kick. For a moment, Sunday’s game was in danger of following a similar script. After taking a 20-6 lead into the fourth quarter, the Seahawks surrendered a 14-play, 82-yard TD drive and then gave the ball right back to Jacksonville following a three-and-out by their offense. Suddenly, the Jaguars had the ball with a chance to mount a game-tying TD drive. But this time, the Seahawks closed it out. Seattle’s defense stymied the Jaguars the rest of the way, holding them to just 17 yards combined over their final three possessions. Darnold then provided the knockout punch, connecting with wide-open tight end AJ Barner for a 61-yard completion that ultimately sealed the victory. AJ Barner in open space for 61 yards! This was also a Jags team that was leading the league in turnover differential (plus-eight) with at least three takeaways in four games this year. Sam Darnold couldn’t throw a pick or fumble, backups in the secondary would be tasked with holding back Jags leading receiver Brian Thomas Jr. (Seattle has lost both games in which they’ve allowed a 100-plus-yard receiver) and would need to get their run game going against a good run defense. Instant Reaction: Seattle Seahawks secure 20-12 road win over Jags The result? Seattle didn’t turn the ball over once, saw an explosive day from Darold and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and bounced back from a Week 5 loss with a win. Here are some extra nuggets from a Week 6 victory. JSN finally gets a win to go with a top performance Smith-Njigba is on pace to smash DK Metcalf’s franchise record for single-season receiving yards. He’s already got more yards through the first six weeks than Metcalf did to begin any season with Seattle, though that’s a credit to Smith-Njigba and not a knock on a spectacular Seahawks career for No. 14. But Sunday’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars also broke an unlucky trend for JSN: his three best single-game performances had all come with losses. That includes 180 yards against the Rams last season (a 26-20 loss in overtime), 132 yards in a 38-35 loss to the Buccaneers last week, and 124 yards to open the season against San Francisco. JSN’s 162 yards in Week 6 are the second-most in any game of his career and the first of over 124 yards to come with a win. Someone hit rewind. 61-yards to the end zone. 🔥 @jaxon_smith1 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/K2SywHB46G — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Darnold remains the league’s most explosive passer Who’d have thought we’d be saying this? Anyone hoping the Seahawks would get a game manager has gotten more than they could’ve dreamed with Darnold’s 2025 campaign so far. Observations from Seahawks’ 20-12 win over Jaguars Entering this game, Darnold and Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones (!) were tied for the most passing plays of 40 or more yards. Both quarterbacks’ teams won today, but Darnold was the only of the two to add on to that explosive-pass-play total. Jones’ longest play of the day was a 26-yarder to Alec Pierce. Darnold had two 61-yard completions against a Jags defense that ranks 27th against the pass, and one of them was a touchdown. Both passes being 61 yards also adds a fun twist on a trend through six games: Darnold’s longest pass completion each and every week has been to Smith-Njigba, but the Ohio State product isn’t in sole possession of that title this week since tight end AJ Barner also snagged one of those two . He made that look wayyy too easy. 🔥 @_ajbarner_ for 61 yards. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/VCEt8fCDPi — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 A Seahawks defense under pressure brings some of its own The Seahawks entered Sunday short three starting defensive backs, including their leader in the secondary in safety Jordan Love. Communication issues popped up on one Jacksonville scoring drive in particular. Busted coverage. Jags score. With arms wiiide open! @BrianThomas_11 | 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/Q9MfrWAOhr — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) October 12, 2025 But the defense didn’t just tighten up; they also continued to bring pressure for a season-high seven sacks (their previous high: six against the Cardinals in Week 4). It continues an impressive effort by the Seahawks’ defense to get sacks without blitzing nearly as much as other teams, and to rack up pressures without having a top player in that category. Byron Murphy II had the most of any Seahawk with nine total pressures through five weeks, well outside players in the top 10 who all have 12 or more. Who do you persistently double team when you’re not quiet sure who could lead the team that day? It’s a bad problem for opposing offenses and a boon for Seattle so far. (AP) Sam Darnold was in the type of groove a quarterback rarely experiences. Then someone told him about it. “Someone at halftime said to me that I hadn't thrown an incompletion,” Darnold said. “So I think he's to blame for throwing an incompletion in the second half.” Whether he believes in jinxes or not, Darnold couldn't feel too disappointed. By the time he threw his first incompletion of the game - early in the third quarter - he'd already tossed four touchdown passes. And his Seattle Seahawks were well on their way to a 38-14 rout of the Washington Commanders on Sunday night. Washington again lost Jayden Daniels to an injury. Daniels, the Commanders' second-year quarterback, left in the fourth quarter after his nonthrowing arm bent gruesomely while he was being tackled near the Seattle goal line. “Just thinking about him and what he's going through right now,” Darnold said after the game. “I just wanted to say that.” Darnold completed his first 17 passes. At halftime, he was 16 for 16 for 282 yards and four TDs against Washington’s beleaguered defense. Rookie Tory Horton had the first two touchdown catches for the Seahawks, and even practice squad elevation Cody White got in on the action before the half was over. It was 31-7 at halftime. Seattle (6-2) remained tied with the Los Angeles Rams atop the NFC West. The Seahawks were without injured receiver Cooper Kupp, but Darnold had plenty of open teammates to throw to. Washington (3-6) lost its fourth straight. Darnold went 21 of 24 for 330 yards before being removed late. The Seahawks took over at their own 10-yard line early on and drove all the way down the field to take the lead on Darnold’s 4-yard scoring pass to Horton. Seattle actually accumulated more than 100 yards of offense on that drive because of penalties. A 25-yard scoring pass to Horton in the second quarter made it 14-0, and after a fumble on the ensuing kickoff, Darnold threw his second TD pass in 11 seconds - 26 yards to Elijah Arroyo. “Just an unacceptable performance by us tonight,” Washington coach Dan Quinn said. “We missed it by a mile.” White’s 60-yard catch-and-run made it 28-0, and after Daniels scored on a 1-yard run with 53 seconds left, Darnold easily drove Seattle into range for a field goal to make it 31-7 at halftime. He threw his first incompletion in the third, and even an interception later that quarter couldn’t do much to dampen Darnold’s night. Daniels, meanwhile, was scrambling around from the start. He rushed for 51 yards but threw for only 153 with an interception. AJ Barner scored on Seattle’s version of a tush push in the third quarter to make it 38-7. Chris Rodriguez scored from 4 yards out for Washington, immediately following Daniels' injury. Darnold became the fourth quarterback since at least 1991 to throw four touchdown passes before his first incompletion. The others were Lamar Jackson in 2019, Ryan Tannehill in 2015 and Tom Brady in 2007, according to Sportradar. “Believe me when I say it: I'm not surprised,” Seattle coach Mike Macdonald said. “We watch Sam every day and how he operates. He's the same guy every day, which is what you love about him. We're chasing it. The guys are determined, and it's fun to watch.” Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 129 yards for the Seahawks. He tied Steve Largent's franchise record with his sixth 100-yard receiving game of the season. At halftime, the Commanders retired Hall of Fame receiver Art Monk's No. 81. Monk caught a then-record 106 passes in 1984, and at one point he was the NFL's career leader in receptions. Monk was with Washington from 1980-93 and played for all three of the franchise's Super Bowl-winning teams. After a handful of games with the Jets and Eagles, he retired with 940 receptions. Seahawks: CB Josh Jobe (concussion) and LB Ernest Jones IV (knee) left the game. Commanders: Washington was without standout WR Terry McLaurin (quadriceps), and then the Commanders lost WR Luke McCaffrey (shoulder) almost immediately. CB Trey Amos (hip) and CB Marshon Lattimore (knee) were also hurt in the game, as was S Quan Martin (hamstring). Of course, Daniels' injury was the most significant. Seahawks: Host Arizona next Sunday. Seattle beat the Cardinals 23-20 in September. Commanders: Host Detroit next Sunday in a rematch of Washington’s victory in last season’s playoffs. --- AP NFL: https://apnews.com/hub/NFL Copyright 2026 STATS LLC and Associated Press. text_body: SEATTLE SEAHAWKS Observations from Seahawks’ 38-14 thrashing of the Commanders Nov 2, 2025, 8:56 PM | Updated: 9:41 pm Seahawks Re-Sign Rashid Shaheed + Free Agency Departures & News - REACTION Hosts Dave Wyman and Bob Stelton (Wyman & Bob) to discuss the news of the first day of NFL Free agency for the Seattle Seahawks, Including the Seahawks resigning Rashid Shaheed and Josh Jobe. That probably won’t be the case any longer. The Seahawks delivered an emphatic statement in front of a national primetime audience Sunday night, racing to a 28-0 first-half lead on their way to a 38-14 road thrashing of the Washington Commanders. Seattle Seahawks win: Instant reaction | Stacy Rost | Recap | Box score With the victory, the Seahawks improved to 6-2 and kept pace with the Los Angeles Rams atop the NFC West. Seattle is now tied with the Rams, the Philadelphia Eagles and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the best record in the NFC. Here’s a look at what stood out from the Seahawks’ blowout win, which could end up being the team’s coming-out party on the national stage. Darnold’s perfect half Sam Darnold, quite literally, was perfect in the first half. Seattle’s new QB1 went a perfect 16-of-16 passing for 282 yards and four touchdowns during a sensational first-half performance, as he continued to showcase that last year’s breakout campaign with the Minnesota Vikings was no one-hit wonder. SAM DARNOLD FOUR TD PASSES IN THE FIRST HALF. SEAvsWAS on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/fax1SUUUBo — NFL (@NFL) November 3, 2025 Darnold was in complete control over those first 30 minutes, carving up Washington’s defense while expertly working through his progressions with precision and decisiveness. According to ESPN’s Brady Henderson , via ESPN Research, Darnold is just the second player since at least 1978 to throw at least four TD passes and no incompletions in a single half. The result was a nearly flawless showing by Seattle’s offense, which racked up 31 points and 330 yards before the break. JSN watch NFL receiving leader Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued his torrid season with another monster performance, hauling in eight receptions for 129 yards – including seven catches for 119 yards in the first half alone. It was Smith-Njigba’s fourth consecutive game with 120-plus receiving yards, making him just the ninth player since the 1970 NFL merger to achieve that feat, according to Stathead. It increased his season total to a league-leading 948 receiving yards, which is the 13th-most in NFL history through the first eight games of a season. And it kept him on pace to break the NFL’s single-season receiving yardage record, set by Detroit’s Calvin Johnson in 2012. Sam Darnold SEAvsWAS on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/TVIpUCzXkW — NFL (@NFL) November 3, 2025 For good measure, Smith-Njigba also had an 11-yard carry and drew a combined 38 penalty yards on a pair of pass-interference flags. And he continued to do it all with a smoothness and repeatability that makes his sheer dominance look almost effortless. No Kupp, no problem The Seahawks were missing their No. 2 receiver in Cooper Kupp, who was sidelined with a pair of injuries. They also were without their fourth and fifth wideouts, with Jake Bobo and Dareke Young also sidelined by injuries. But the offense didn’t miss a beat. In addition to another sensational night from Smith-Njigba, several other players rose to the occasion with big plays. TORY HORTON AGAIN. SEAvsWAS on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/5hHRO65o7N — NFL (@NFL) November 3, 2025 Rookie wideout Tory Horton had pair of touchdown catches, including a 25-yarder where he raced past cornerback Mike Sainristil with an excellent release off the line of scrimmage. Horton now has five TD receptions through the first eight games of his career. Rookie tight end Elijah Arroyo hauled in a 26-yard scoring grab for his first career touchdown. And wide receiver Cody White, who was elevated off the practice squad, also found the end zone for the first time in his career, scoring on a 60-yard catch-and-run that gave Seattle a 28-0 first-half lead. Defense and special teams do their part Darnold, JSN & Co. understandably received the bulk of the attention Sunday night. But Seattle’s defense and special teams certainly did their part as well. The Seahawks turned in another stellar defensive showing, limiting the Commanders to just seven points through the first three quarters and just 290 total yards for the game. Their pass rush recorded four sacks and provided constant pressure on Daniels. And they came up with a key takeaway in the second quarter, when Devon Witherspoon shot through a gap on a cornerback blitz and forced an off-balanced throw by Daniels, whose pass was picked off by safety Ty Okada on a spectacular leaping sideline interception. Ty Okada picks off Daniels on 3rd & 17 SEAvsWAS on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/BtR6QSlRyG — NFL (@NFL) November 3, 2025 Not to be outdone, the Seahawks’ kick coverage unit delivered a key play in the second quarter, when Brandon Pili forced a fumble and Connor O’Toole recovered it at the Washington 26-yard line to give Seattle’s offense a short field. Darnold and Arroyo then connected for a TD pass on the very next play to make it 21-0, and the rout was on. Seattle Seahawks Inactives: WR Cooper Kupp out vs Commanders Follow @CameronVanTil

title: Sam Darnold ‘Just Ridiculous’ In Seahawks’ Dominant Week 9 Win Over Washington
text_body: Sam Darnold 'Just Ridiculous' In Seahawks' Dominant Week 9 Win Over Washington Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold had a flawless first half to help lead the Seahawks to a big road win over the Commanders. Nov 03, 2025 at 12:42 AM John Boyle Seahawks.com Senior Reporter Copied! LANDOVER, Md.—Sam Darnold knew he and the Seahawks offense were functioning well in the first half. Darnold just didn't know quite how well he was playing—he was perfect, statistically—until someone pointed it out to him in the locker room at halftime. In leading the Seahawks to a 38-14 win over the Commanders, Darnold completed all 16 pass attempts in the first half for 282 yards, including four touchdowns—two to rookie receiver Tory Horton and one each to tight end Elijah Arroyo and receiver Cody White—as the Seahawks built a 31-7 halftime lead. Then in the locker room, someone told Darnold about his hot streak, which, if you're the type who believes in jinxes, could very well explain why his second attempt of the third quarter was an incomplete pass on third-and-short, leading to Seattle's first punt of the game. " Obviously, I can feel the flow of the game and understand that we're doing really good on offense, but no, I didn't know that I hadn't thrown an incompletion," Darnold said. "It's pretty cool. Someone at halftime said to me that I hadn't thrown an incompletion, so I think he's to blame for throwing an incompletion in the second half." Darnold would not reveal who told him the news, saying with a grin, "I'm not going to say who it was." Darnold's 17 consecutive completions tied a franchise record set by Warren Moon, and was about as good of stretch of passing that Darnold could remember since his days at San Clemente High School. "I've got to go back to the archives for that," Darnold said. "I think I had a similar game in high school, but college or pro, that's probably the most consecutively." Not long after the first incompletion, Darnold had his first real mistake of the game, throwing behind Cody White while rolling to his left on third down, leading to an interception, but he bounced right back from that to lead a touchdown drive that removed any shred of suspense from the game. In all, Darnold completed 21 of 24 passes for 330 yards and four touchdowns, giving him a 141.0 passer rating, his second game this season with at least 300 yards and four touchdowns, and his fifth in the last six games with a rating of 111.4 or better. "Sam's execution right now, it's just ridiculous," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. "All the things we talked about that he's been doing—decisive, making smart decisions." And as great as Darnold was, Macdonald wasn't surprised to see his quarterback put up such impressive numbers. "Believe me when I say, I'm not surprised," Macdonald said. "We watched Sam every day on how he operates, and he's the same guy every day, which is what you love about him. And we're chasing it. The guys are determined, and it's fun to watch. And when the team comes together, that's this type of stuff that you can do when you play the right way, you prepare the right way. And our coaches deserve a lot of credit too, man. I thought (Offensive Coordinator) Klint (Kubiak) called a great game. All the coaches involved in the game plan process, I thought we had some great answers, and it all came together." Darnold opened his day by leading a 90-yard touchdown drive, one that saw the Seahawks overcome three penalties for 25 yards on the possession, including a 15-yarder that set up first-and-25. He capped the drive with a touchdown to rookie Tory Horton, who was starting in place of an injured Cooper Kupp, and Darnold would go on to lead the Seahawks to four touchdowns on their first four possessions while going 5 for 5 on third down in the first half. "Sam, he plays with that chip on his shoulder, he's always bringing his A game, and you can tell how bad he wants it," Horton said. "From the whole week of preparing, we knew he was going to be dialed in. He's one hell of a quarterback, he's on fire right now." Added Cody White, who had a 60-yard touchdown, "He's playing great football right now. We can't ask for anything more." The Seahawks What The Seahawks Said Following Their 38-14 Win At The Commanders Rapid Reactions: Sam Darnold & Seahawks Offense Dominate In Sunday Night Win At Washington Full Highlights: Seahawks at Commanders As they so often have this season, Darnold and the offense benefited from some short fields thanks to the defense and special teams units doing their part. Safety Ty Okada had an interception that gave the Seahawks the ball at their own 40-yard line, good field position they'd turn into a touchdown, then not long after, the Seahawks forced a turnover on special teams, setting up a one-play touchdown drive, with Darnold hitting Elijah Arroyo with a perfectly-placed pass for the rookie's first career touchdown. While the defense enjoys getting stops and plays to set the offense up for success, those players also enjoy watching Darnold go to work once they're off the field. "I feel like he's kind of been in the zone all season," said defensive end Leonard Williams. "It's been special for us to watch on offense. It's just amazing to have a good defense, get off the field, then just have such complementary football when the offense takes the field and can drive down the field. We're just watching from the sidelines in amazement." Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had eight catches for 129 yards for his sixth 100-yard game catching passes from Darnold this season, said of Darnold. "Man, he's just a pro. I love playing with him. He's going to be ready throughout the week. He's going to make sure his troops are ready. He's going go out there and execute. He's going to play his hardest. That's all you can ask, you know. He's just playing and giving his heart up, putting it all out there on the field. We're all going to follow him. He's just been so great for us." The Seattle Seahawks followed up last week’s primetime rout of the Washington Commanders with another first-half onslaught, as they steamrolled to a 44-22 shellacking of the NFC West rival Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon at Lumen Field. Seattle Seahawks win: Instant Reaction | Stacy Rost | Recap | Box Score The Seahawks raced to a 35-0 lead by the midway point of the second quarter and matched a franchise record with 38 first-half points en route to another massive statement that’s sure to place the rest of the NFL on notice. With the victory, Seattle improved to 7-2 and remained tied atop the NFC West with the Los Angeles Rams. The Seahawks and Rams meet for the first of their two divisional showdowns next week in Los Angeles. Here’s what stood out from Seattle’s dismantling of the Cardinals. Another fast start The Seahawks are turning these first-half beatdowns into a common occurrence. In Week 3, the Seahawks raced to a 38-6 halftime lead in a rout of the New Orleans Saints. Last week, they built a 31-7 halftime lead in a primetime blowout of the Commanders. And on Sunday, they stormed to a 38-7 halftime lead over the Cardinals. AZvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/rdrh4DKds9 — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2025 With those three performances, Seattle is now responsible for three of the four highest-scoring first halves in the NFL this season, according to Pro Football Focus . The only other team to score at least 31 points in the first half of a game this year is the Minnesota Vikings, who scored 34 first-half points against the Cincinnati Bengals. Pass rush wreaks havoc again Seattle’s stellar pass rush had yet another dominant performance. It was highlighted by two nearly identical first-half defensive touchdowns. In both cases, second-year linebacker Tyrice Knight burst through Arizona’s offensive line on a blitz and knocked the ball free from backup quarterback Jacoby Brissett. And in both cases, veteran defensive end DeMarcus Lawrence scooped up the loose ball and ran it back for a score. DEMARCUS LAWRENCE SCOOP-N-SCORE! AZvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/u8zHFcadls — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2025 Knight’s two strip-sack fumbles led a five-sack first half for Seattle. Defensive lineman Leonard Williams and edge rusher Boye Mafe each added one sack apiece, while Lawrence and rookie safety Nick Emmanwori each chipped in a half-sack. Seattle recorded a 42.3% pressure rate in the first half, according to PFF , and limited Brissett to just 11-of-22 passing over the first 30 minutes. JSN maintains historic pace NFL receiving leader Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued his torrid season with another big game. The 2023 first-round pick hauled in five receptions for 93 yards and a touchdown, including four catches for 82 yards and a TD in the first quarter. Smith-Njigba increased his season total to 1,041 receiving yards, which is the fifth-most through the first nine games of a season by any player since the 1970 NFL merger, according to Stathead . Smith-Njigba also had back-to-back receptions of 17 yards and 14 yards on Seattle’s ensuing touchdown drive later in the first quarter. Less-heralded defenders lay the boom The Seahawks dealt a slew of punishing hits on Sunday. And the biggest ones came from some of their less-heralded players. One week after his first career interception, safety Ty Okada delivered a bone-rattling hit over the middle on tight end Elijah Higgins that resulted in a third-down pass breakup. Okada, who has been filling in for the injured Julian Love, also brought down running back Zonovan Knight for a fourth-and-goal stop at the 1-yard line. The Seahawks scored the game’s first 35 points, including two nearly identical defensive touchdowns , and steamrolled the Arizona Cardinals 44-22 in an NFC West matchup on Sunday at Lumen Field. Seattle Seahawks win: Observations | Stacy Rost | Recap | Box Score The Seahawks improved to 7-2 with the victory and kept pace with the Los Angeles Rams for the best record in their division and the NFC. The 6-2 Philadelphia Eagles, who play Monday night, are the only other two-loss team with at least six wins in the NFC. Here are the instant reactions to Sunday’s game from some of the voices of Seattle Sports, including Seahawks Radio Network analyst Dave Wyman’s thoughts in the video at the top of this post. Brock Huard – Brock & Salk (6-10 a.m. weekdays) #Seahawks win 44-22, @BrockHuard shares his instant reaction. 👇 RECAP 📰: https://t.co/gJbsLnUY4X pic.twitter.com/8WakeUjWRK — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) November 10, 2025 Bob Stelton – Wyman & Bob (2-7 p.m. weekdays) This game was pretty much what you would have expected coming in. The Seahawks are just a better team than the Cardinals, and they showed that right out of the gate. You couldn’t have asked for a better first half of football – their best of the season! They put up 38 points thanks in large part to two fumbles forced by Tyrice Knight that resulted in both being recovered for touchdowns by DeMarcus Lawrence. The second half was definitely a bit of a step back with some sloppy play and turnovers. They scored just six points on two field goals in the second half. But they were so dominate and built such a substantial lead early that you don’t really worry about that. The interesting stat in this is the rushing attempts versus the passing attempts – 46 rushing attempts for 198 yards (a season high) and two TDs to just 12 pass attempts in the entire game for 178 yards and one TD. This team is rolling through the teams you feel they should beat, and the big test comes in the next game against an equally hot Los Angeles Rams team. That will be the game to truly measure just how good this Hawks team is. Running it up. 📈 +6 @zachcharbon 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/c7Yb6RON3e — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 9, 2025 Mike Lefko – Wyman & Bob A thoroughly dominant performance by the Seahawks’ defense and an impressive win for the totality of domination that Seattle inflicted on Arizona in the first half. The Seahawks keep losing critical players on defense yet continue to perform at a high level. Nothing embodies the “next man up” mentality like linebacker Tyrice Knight, who lost his starting spot earlier this season and stepped up in a massive win Sunday with two forced fumbles that went for defensive touchdowns. The same can be said for safety Ty Okada and a couple of big hits and passes defended that he had today. You would have never known that this team was missing starters at all three levels of the defense. It was essentially a shutout for the Seahawks’ defense: the only points allowed came on turnovers that gave the Cardinals the ball right in front of the Seattle end zone and when the game was fully out of reach. And those early touchdowns came after the defense had stopped Arizona’s offense twice on fourth-and-goal. About as impressive of a performance as we have seen from a Mike Macdonald defense, and it’s a large sample size at this point. You can nitpick the offense being sloppy with the ball, but those turnovers came after a 35-0 lead and the understandable inclination to subconsciously relax with that kind of margin. One undeniably good sign from the Seahawks was the rushing attack being able to put the game away with two time-consuming, yardage-eating drives in the second half. They were unable to do that in the first matchup against the Cardinals, and it almost cost them. Today, they asserted their will on the ground when they needed to do so. And now, the focus fully turns to the game of the season and the most important one in Mike Macdonald’s tenure: the 7-2 Seahawks versus the 7-2 Rams. Name a more iconic duo… we'll wait. 😏 @Tyricek_ @TankLawrence 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/3aBULHVUD9 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 9, 2025 More on the Seattle Seahawks • Deja vu: Seattle Seahawks score 2 nearly identical defensive TDs • Watch: Seattle Seahawks put Cardinals in early hole with 2 quick TDs • Brock: An underrated Seattle Seahawks pivot ‘paying big dividends’ Wyman & Bob Brock and Salk podcast

San Francisco 49ers 2025 Schedule Release | Golden Trail Click here to purchase tickets The San Francisco 49ers have announced their 2025 regular season schedule along with the opponents and date ranges for the team's three preseason games. A Closer Look at the 2025 Schedule… San Francisco will open the regular season on the road (at Seattle) for the fourth time in five seasons and for the first time since visiting the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1 of the 2023 season. The 49ers open the season on the road against an NFC West opponent for the first time since the 2010 season when they visited Seattle in Week 1. The Niners open the season against an NFC West opponent for the first time since the 2020 season when they hosted the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1. text_body: RAMS Rams hold on to beat Seahawks, 21-19: Instant analysis of Week 11 thriller The Rams won a nail biter to take over the lead in the NFC West Cameron DaSilva Rams Wire Updated Nov. 16, 2025, 5:42 p.m. PT It was always going to be a battle. No one expected the Los Angeles Rams or Seattle Seahawks to blow out the other team in this game. And sure enough, it was close throughout from start to finish. The Rams were in control for most of the afternoon but the Seahawks refused to go away and let Los Angeles run away with the win. The Rams' biggest lead was 14-3 in the first quarter after scoring on two of their first three possessions, with the only exception being a turnover on downs on their opening drive. The offense stalled from the second quarter on and never had a drive longer than 25 yards in the final three quarters, but the defense kept Los Angeles in the game with four interceptions of Sam Darnold. And that was without Quentin Lake on the field for the second half after he suffered an elbow injury . The Rams shut down Darnold and the league's third-highest-scoring offense in the league, allowing just 19 points – well below Seattle's 30-point average. In the end, the Rams defense held strong one last time on the Seahawks' final drive, preventing Seattle from scoring any points and preventing a 21-19 lead in the final minutes after the offense failed to put the game away. Final score: Rams 21, Seahawks 19 Numbers to know 1,000: Davante Adams became the 17th player in NFL history to catch 1,000 passes in his career, and it came on his first-quarter touchdown – his 10th score of the season. 30: In the first quarter alone, Kyren Williams broke off two runs of 30-plus yards, one for 30 and another for 34 yards. He had just one 30-yard run all of last year. 3: Nate Landman forced yet another fumble, his third straight game with a punch-out. Unfortunately, the Rams were unable to recover the loose ball. 2: Kamren Kinchens picked off Sam Darnold twice in the game, giving him four interceptions against the Seahawks in the last two seasons. 4: The Rams intercepted Darnold four times in this game, which matches their most interceptions in a game this century. It's their most since their four picks against the Broncos in 2022. 1: Only one player on the Rams had more than two catches, and it was Puka Nacua, who hauled in seven passes for 75 yards. 165: The Seahawks had 165 more yards than the Rams in this one but only scored one touchdown. 22:11: The Rams only had the ball for 22:11 in this game, allowing the Seahawks to have 37:49 time of possession. It was over when… ... Jason Myers' 61-yard field goal sailed wide right of the uprights, giving the Rams a 21-19 win. 3 stars of the game Kamren Kinchens: 4 tackles, 2 interceptions Puka Nacua: 7 catches, 75 yards. 2 carries, 18 yards Kyren Williams: 12 carries, 91 yards, 1 TD. 1 catch, 5 yards Play of the game Ethan Evans may not get much attention on a team that's so good on offense and defense, but his punt late in the fourth quarter pinned the Seahawks at the 1-yard line. That forced the Seahawks to go a long way in order to kick a potential game-winning field goal. What's next? The Rams have another big game on their schedule coming up, a Sunday night matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 12. Their recent schedule has been a gauntlet of NFC contenders and Los Angeles is trying to establish itself as the best of the bunch. Kickoff next Sunday is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. INGLEWOOD, Calif. – It took every one of the Rams secondary's four interceptions, and every last second of regulation, for the Rams to hang on for a 21-19 win over the Seahawks on Sunday at SoFi Stadium. The victory moved the Rams (8-2) into first place in the NFC West and extended their win streak to five games. Leading 21-19 with 2:23 remaining after Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III's 1-yard rushing touchdown, the Rams got the Seahawks down to one timeout with 1:51 remaining, but couldn't convert the 3rd and 10 from their own 49. However, punter Ethan Evans ' ensuing kick traveled 50 yards and landed out of bounds at the Seahawks' own 1-yard line. Seattle moved into position at the end of the ensuing series for a 61-yard try by kicker Jason Myers with one second left, but Myers missed short. Safety Kamren Kinchens accounted for two of Los Angeles' four interceptions, and both directly lead to touchdown scoring drives by L.A.'s offense against Seattle (7-3). Cornerbacks Cobie Durant and Darious Williams each had one. Running back Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 91 yards and one touchdown in the win, cracking the Top 10 in franchise history in rushing yards with his performance. He had carries of 30 and 34 yards in the game, the latter marking Williams' longest of the season. Safety Quentin Lake left the game in the first half with an elbow injury and did not return. Tight end Tyler Higbee left the game in the second half with an ankle injury. Here is the complete game recap: The Rams went for it on 4th and 1 from the Seahawks 8 after a failed challenge, but that opening drive ended after an incomplete pass by quarterback Matthew Stafford that was intended for tight end Tyler Higbee. (AP) — The Rams made four interceptions and they kept Seattle out of the end zone for the first 57 1/2 minutes. Los Angeles’ offense scored three touchdowns against the Seahawks’ vaunted defense. Los Angeles Rams 21, Seattle Seahawks 19: Box Score This meeting of streaking NFC West powers still came down to a long field goal attempt as time expired. When Jason Myers came up short and wide right from 61 yards, the Rams celebrated a messy victory — but one with season-defining potential. “We’re never going to apologize for being able to find ways to win,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. Kamren Kinchens had two of the Rams’ four picks, Matthew Stafford threw two touchdown passes and Los Angeles hung on to beat the Seahawks 21-19 Sunday for its fifth consecutive victory. Davante Adams had his 10th touchdown catch and Kyren Williams rushed for 91 yards and a score for the Rams (8-2), who made up for an uncharacteristically tepid offensive performance by forcing Sam Darnold into his first four-interception game since 2019. The Seahawks still made a furious late rally that might have ended in their own fifth consecutive victory — if not for a spectacular punt. The Rams were looking good with a nine-point lead and six minutes to play, but Seattle had an 84-yard drive ending in Kenneth Walker III’s touchdown dive with 2:23 to play. Kenneth Walker scores and cuts it to a one-score game 👀 SEAvsLAR on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/1w9alTFUuO — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2025 Seattle’s defense got a quick stop, but Ethan Evans’ 50-yard punt bounced with surreal perfection at the Seattle 1 with 1:41 left. Darnold shook off his rough afternoon and got the Seahawks to midfield with help from a pass interference penalty. Rashid Shaheed then slid for a catch at the Los Angeles 43 and was allowed to call a timeout with 1 second on the clock. Myers made four earlier field goals, but couldn’t hit a kick that would have matched his career long. “We’re about 3 yards short from putting ourselves in a great position to go win, given all the things that happened throughout the game,” Seattle coach Mike Macdonald said. Darnold passed for 279 yards for the Seahawks (7-3), whose remarkable 10-game road winning streak ended with their first loss outside Seattle since September 2024. “We were still in this, despite the turnovers and all of the things that happened,” Darnold said. “And that’s a huge credit to our defense, the way that they played all day. I just wish I could have played better for our defense and just everyone on the team.” Kinchens equaled his two-interception performance in the Rams’ similarly wild overtime win at Seattle last season, while Cobie Durant and Darious Williams also had picks in the second half. They want to keep trying us, then they’ll keep seeing it.” Starting with Kinchens’ interception on Seattle’s third snap, Darnold had another nightmare afternoon against the Rams’ defense. The USC product and Orange County native struggled against LA twice last season with the Minnesota Vikings, getting sacked nine times in the Rams’ playoff win. Cooper Kupp had three fourth-quarter catches in his first game against the Rams following eight seasons as a prolific receiver for Los Angeles. Fans of both teams in the stadium where he won the Super Bowl 56 MVP award serenaded Kupp with chants of “Coooop” when he finally got his hands on the ball late. Stafford passed for a season-low 130 yards while the Rams managed just 249 yards against Seattle’s vaunted defense, compared to the Seahawks’ 414 — but Los Angeles still hasn’t trailed since Week 6. “We found a way to win without playing perfect football against a really good team,” Stafford said. “Our defense played outstanding. They deserve to be partying like crazy.” Adams scored on his 1,000th career reception and former Seahawks tight end Colby Parkinson caught a 6-yard TD pass early in the fourth quarter for the Rams, who didn’t have a drive longer than 25 net yards in the final three quarters. TENTH tuddy of the year for Tae! 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/zoznoYn47s — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 16, 2025 Jaxon Smith-Njigba had nine catches for 105 yards, becoming the first player in the Super Bowl era to have 75 yards receiving in each of his team’s first 10 games. The Rams ran only three offensive plays in the second quarter, but Seattle had to settle for field goals after a 13-play drive and another 15-play drive. The Rams’ offense continued to sputter until Darnold threw into double coverage for Kinchens’ second interception late in the third quarter. Parkinson scored moments later. text_body: New Orleans Saints 2025 Season Recap | Game-by-Game Dive into the New Orleans Saints' 2025 NFL season, featuring game-by-game recaps, highlights, photos, game notes, and key moments. Jan 05, 2026 at 11:15 AM New Orleans Saints Copied! Michael C. Hebert/New Orleans Saints The New Orleans Saints finished the season 6-11, in fourth place in the NFC South, in Kellen Moore's first year as head coach of the Saints. The team started the season with quarterback Spencer Rattler as the starter getting out to a 1-7 start through Week 8. The team then handed the keys to rookie quarterback Tyler Shough and finished the remainder of the season 5-4. Here's a game-by-game breakdown of the Saints' 2025 NFL season. Saints vs. Cardinals | 2025 NFL Week 1 WHEN/WHERE: Sept. 7, 2025 at Caesars Superdome, New Orleans, LA RESULT: Cardinals 20, Saints 13 RECORD: (0-1) 🏈 GAME RECAP | 📸 GAME PHOTOS | 🎥 GAME HIGHLIGHTS | 📝 GAME NOTES GAME SUMMARY A few big plays from the Arizona Cardinals and a slew of penalties by the New Orleans Saints led to a 20-13 Arizona victory in Sunday's season-opener at the Caesars Superdome. The game marked the debut of Coach Kellen Moore and it ended a streak of six consecutive opening game victories for the Saints. New Orleans had a chance to tie the score but its final possession end with an incompletion on fourth-and-10 from the 18-yard line. FULL GAME RECAP GAME NOTES & STATS New Orleans outgained Arizona in yards 315-276. The Saints had 208 net passing yards and 107 rushing yards. The Saints had 21 first downs compared to Arizona's 19. Running back Alvin Kamara led the backfield with 45 yards on 11 rushes and one 18-yard rushing touchdown. He also had two catches for 12 yards. With Kamara's 45 rushing yards, he surpasses Wilbert Montgomery and Robert Smith for 75th all-time (6,824) in NFL record books, and his 12 receiving yards passes LaDainian Tomlinson for 13th all-time for running backs (4,774). Kamara's touchdown in the second quarter was the 1,000th by the team in the Caesars Superdome regular season and postseason combined since 1975. The Saints are the third team all-time to do it, joining the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field (1,114 prior to Green Bay's late afternoon game) and the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium (1,029). The Buffalo Bills have 998 at Highmark Stadium. Defensive end Cameron Jordan finished with three tackles, including 1.5 sacks for 14.5 yards, two stops for loss and one pass deflection. Jordan now has 123 career sacks, surpassing Clyde Simmons and Simeon Rice, and tying Robert Mathis for 20th all-time in NFL record books. FULL GAME RECAP GAME NOTES & STATS Quarterback Spencer Rattler went 25-for-34 (career-high 73.5 pct.) for 206 yards, threw a career-high three touchdown passes and recorded a 118.1 passer rating. This was his first time throwing multiple touchdowns in a game in his career. He also rushed four times for 14 yards. Running back Alvin Kamara recorded 99 rushing yards, surpassing Curt Warner, Antowain Smith and Rodney Hampton to be 72nd all-time in NFL record books. He also caught six passes for 21 yards. Defensive end Chris Rumph II stripped the ball from San Francisco QB Mac Jones and LB Demario Davis recovered to record New Orleans' first takeaway of the regular season for the ninth of his career. It was Rumph's first career forced fumble. Jordan played in his 228th career regular season game, which tied QB Drew Brees for most games played in club history. He also moved into sole possession of 13th place in NFL record books among defensive lineman today, surpassing Jim Jeffcoat. It was the first victory of Coach Kellen Moore's tenure and the first win for Spencer Rattler as the team's starting quarterback as the Saints improved to 1-4. The loss dropped the Giants to 1-4. FULL GAME RECAP GAME NOTES & STATS Coach Kellen Moore received his first victory against the Giants. Quarterback Spencer Rattler went 21-for-31 for 225 yards with one touchdown, zero interceptions and a 99.5 passer rating. Rattler also rushed five times for 22 yards. He had 187 yards passing in the first half, the most in a half in his career. It also marks Rattler's first win as a starting quarterback in the NFL, and the first time that a quarterback drafted by the Saints started and recorded a win since Danny Wuerffel (9/13/98 19-14 win vs. Carolina at Caesars Superdome). The receiving effort was led by Rashid Shaheed, who recorded four receptions for 114 yards (28.5 avg.) and a touchdown. Receiver Chris Olave also put up seven receptions for 59 yards. The 87-yard bomb from Rattler to Shaheed was the longest play from scrimmage since an 87-yard touchdown connection from Drew Brees to Brandin Cooks vs. Carolina, 10/16/16. It is tied for the fifth-longest play in franchise history. Kamara surpassed Tiki Barber and Marcus Allen to move into fifth place all-time in NFL record books for receptions by a running back. Drake Maye, New England's second-year quarterback, completed three long touchdown passes and the Patriots added a field goal to give them enough points to improve to 4-2. He finished 15-of-24 (62.5 pct.) for 176 yards to go with one second quarter touchdown pass to tight end Juwan Johnson and one interception. Quarterback Taysom Hill added four carries for 30 yards including a season-best/team-high 29-yard run. The most Seattle had ever beaten the franchise by was 20 points (against the then-Oilers) back in 1979. Surely this year’s top-five scoring unit could do the same? Seahawks beat Titans | Observations | Instant Reaction | Stats Unfortunately not. It was a final of 30-24, though Seattle did lead by 20 twice in the third quarter. Still, a win’s a win, and Seattle added another to the column in a tight NFC race. “Our guys showed a lot of resilience,” Mike Macdonald told reporters after the game. “Obviously would’ve liked to close the game out earlier, but our guys fought really hard. You don’t play team’s records in this league. Teams are too talented … (The Titans) had a lot of one-score games that haven’t gone their way and today’s one of them. Hats off to them.” The defense is banged up and looked like it. Seattle’s defense has been stellar all season and given its rash of injuries, particularly at linebacker and safety, you can hardly knock it for a shakier day against the Titans. But it’s still an easy takeaway against a Titans team that’s averaged just over 14 points per game and scored their most of the season (24) against Seattle. It’s worth noting the defense didn’t allow all 24 points; there was a Titans punt return touchdown as well. Does it matter? Not really, at least assuming starters like Ernest Jones IV (knee) and, eventually, Julian Love (on injured reserve) are able to return when it matters most. Credit a few backups for having a big day in relief — guys like Patrick O’Connell, who had one of Seattle’s four sacks today. “We have an ongoing joke that we can’t block Patty-O on a daily basis,” Macdonald said of O’Connell’s day postgame. “Excited to watch the tape and see how he did.” A zero turnover game with a few turnover-worthy plays. Week 12 marked just the second time this season Seattle’s offense did not turn the ball over in a game (at Jacksonville was the first). That’s great! Especially for a team that’s leading the league in giveaways. But the play on the field wasn’t as clean as it looked in the box score. In addition to a few miscues and overthrows, a deep incompletion by Sam Darnold was very nearly (and probably should have been) picked off by Titans cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. Still, it’s a step. Given the first takeaway, here’s what matters: if Seattle’s defense can’t get healthier by next week, the offense is going to need to play cleaner football. A big-time play by a backup linebacker is great; more conversions and positive plays in the red zone by Seattle against a bad defense does more. The Titans’ 32nd-ranked offense outpaced Seattle in red-zone conversions, fourth-down conversions and third-down conversions. History-maker, record-breaker. With an 8-yard reception in the third quarter, Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba broke DK Metcalf’s franchise record for single-season receiving yards (1,303). JSN breaks Seattle Seahawks’ season receiving record – in just 11 games Smith-Njigba is at 1,313 on the season with six (!) games left to play. That outpaces the production of the current league-wide record holder for single-season receiving yards, Calvin Johnson. It’s a fun reminder that Johnson’s final seven games of the season back in 2012 saw jaw-dropping production. title: Xavier Restrepo first NFL catch comes on signature Cam Ward play vs Seahawks
text_body: Story by The Tennessean Nick Gray, Nashville Tennessean Sun, Nov 23, 2025 · 2 min read Add Yahoo Sports on Google Xavier Restrepo waited until the fourth quarter of his first game to make his first NFL catch, and it came on a signature play by his college and-now-pro quarterback for the Tennessee Titans against the Seattle Seahawks on Nov. 23. Cam Ward avoided one defender, then found Restrepo in the middle of the field for a 14-yard gain as the rookie quarterback was being hit out of bounds at Nissan Stadium. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ward has shown the ability to make these kinds of plays outside of the pocket, keeping his eyes downfield and showing a fearlessness in throwing across the field to an open receiver. Add it to Ward's highlight reel, and start one for Restrepo. CANES CONNECTION @CanesFootball 🙌 @Cameron7Ward escapes and finds @xavierrestrepo1 for the first down! 📺: #SEAvsTEN on @NFLonFOX & NFL+ pic.twitter.com/neQ6Xpssnp — Tennessee Titans (@Titans) November 23, 2025 Restrepo was featured some in the second half at receiver as the Titans ' evolving receiver rotation continued on against Seattle. His first target came with him in the end zone on what was an incomplete pass. The undrafted free agent out of Miami who set a program record for career receiving yards was elevated from the practice squad for the Week 12 game after Calvin Ridley was lost for the season last week and Elic Ayomanor was ruled out with a hamstring injury during the week. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I was supposed to have that one in the end zone," Restrepo said after the game. "I was kind of pissed off about that, if I’m gonna be honest. But honestly, Cam let me know that he’s going to come back to me. That’s why he’s not only a great quarterback, but a great leader as well. The trust barrier between us two is there always." GENTRY ESTES: All these Titans losses are starting to look the same The Titans drive did sputter out for no points after a sack and a holding penalty in the eventual 30-24 loss, but the Ward off-script highlights continue to pile up in his rookie season. Seahawks win: Instant Reaction | Stacy Rost’s Takeaways | Recap | Box Score With the victory, the Seahawks improved to 9-3 and moved back into a first-place tie atop the NFC West – thanks to the Carolina Panthers’ upset win over the Los Angeles Rams earlier in the day. The Rams still hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over Seattle, but the Seahawks have a Week 16 rematch next month to nullify that. Here’s what stood out from Seattle’s first shutout since Week 3 of 2015. Ball-hawking defense overwhelms Vikings On paper, it was a mismatch. Seattle’s defense is one of the league’s best, while Minnesota’s offense is one of the league’s worst. And on top of that, the Vikings were missing quarterback J.J. McCarthy, left tackle Christian Darrisaw and rookie left guard Donovan Jackson due to injuries. Filling in for McCarthy was undrafted rookie quarterback Max Brosmer, who was making his first career start. On the field, it played out about as expected. Seattle’s defense completely overwhelmed the shorthanded Vikings, limiting them to just 162 total yards while picking off Brosmer four times and finishing with a season-high five takeaways. Ernest Jones IV had two interceptions – including an 85-yard pick-six – to give him a team-high five interceptions this year. Coby Bryant and Riq Woolen also snagged interceptions, and DeMarcus Lawrence forced a fumble that Ty Okada recovered. For as great as their defense has been, the Seahawks entered the day with just 13 takeaways through their first 11 games. They increased that number in a major way on Sunday. WHAT JUST HAPPENED‼️ 85 yards to the house. #ProBowlVote + @ernestjones 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/AHKHvIhouE — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 30, 2025 D-Law’s big day Three weeks ago, Lawrence was the beneficiary of a pair of strip-sack fumbles by Tyrice Knight, returning both of them for a pair of touchdowns that broke open blowout victory over the Arizona Cardinals. On Sunday, it was Lawrence who served as the instigator for a pair of Seahawks takeaways – including a game-swinging defensive score. With Minnesota facing fourth-and-1 on the Seattle 4-yard line late in the first half, Lawrence came unblocked off the edge and pressured Brosmer into a game-changing mistake. As Brosmer was backpedaling and being pulled to the ground, he flung an underhanded, desperation heave into traffic that Jones intercepted and returned for an 85-yard pick-six. That gave the Seahawks a 10-0 lead and swung the game firmly back into their control. Watch: Seahawks return INT for TD on wild play Lawrence struck again in the third quarter, when he caught up to running back Aaron Jones Sr. and knocked the ball free from behind for a fumble that Okada recovered. Lawrence also had a sack and a tackle for loss, continuing an impressive age-33 season for the four-time Pro Bowl defensive end. He now has 5.0 sacks and nine tackles for loss in 11 games this year. DEFENSE IS COOKING ‼️ @TankLawrence @tyokada 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/ix0jcuRwUs — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 30, 2025 Pass protection struggles The Seahawks had done a great job of protecting Sam Darnold this season, having allowed an NFL-low 11 sacks through their first 11 games. But the Vikings came in with the league’s highest blitz rate and the second-highest pressure rate, according to Pro Football Reference. And sure enough, Minnesota’s pass rush was a problem for Seattle. The Vikings sacked Darnold four times in the first half, including a strip-sack fumble that set up Minnesota in the red zone and another strip-sack fumble that Seattle recovered. The other two first-half sacks came on third down, ending a pair of Seahawks drives. The Vikings also pressured Darnold into a third-down throwaway and knocked down several passes at the line of scrimmage. As a result, Seattle struggled to move the ball for much of the afternoon. The Seahawks were held to a season-low 219 total yards and mustered just four field goals over their first eight possessions until Zach Charbonnet found the end zone on a 17-yard TD run in the fourth quarter. But on a day when their defense completely dominated, that was still more than enough offense for the Seahawks. Seahawks place Holani on IR, sign Gaskin to active roster Follow @CameronVanTil
